Let the square have side $s$, with its sides making angle $\alpha\in[0,\pi/2]$ with the horizontal. The vertical span of the square is $s(\sin\alpha+\cos\alpha)$, which equals $3d$ (the height from $A$ to $C$). Set $H=s(\sin\alpha+\cos\alpha)=3d$.

**Vertices.** Taking $A=(0,0)$ with side directions $(\cos\alpha,\sin\alpha)$ and $(-\sin\alpha,\cos\alpha)$:
$$A=(0,0),\ B=s(\cos\alpha,\sin\alpha),\ C=s(\cos\alpha-\sin\alpha,\,\sin\alpha+\cos\alpha),\ D=s(-\sin\alpha,\cos\alpha).$$
The $y$-coordinates are $0,\ s\sin\alpha,\ H,\ s\cos\alpha$. Define $r=\dfrac{\sin\alpha}{\sin\alpha+\cos\alpha}\in[0,\tfrac12]$ (using symmetry $r\leftrightarrow 1-r$). Then the breakpoints are at $y=rH$ and $y=(1-r)H$.

**Cross-section width** $w(y)$ of the square (a symmetric trapezoid profile):
- $y\in[0,rH]$: $w(y)=\dfrac{y}{\sin\alpha\cos\alpha}$ (rising),
- $y\in[rH,(1-r)H]$: $w(y)=\dfrac{s}{\cos\alpha}$ (flat),
- $y\in[(1-r)H,H]$: $w(y)=\dfrac{H-y}{\sin\alpha\cos\alpha}$ (falling).

**Area probability for $P$.** The zone between $L_2,L_3$ is $y\in[H/3,\,2H/3]$, the middle third. Using the symmetry $w(y)=w(H-y)$:

For $r\in[1/3,1/2]$ (the relevant range, as verified below), the zone spans all three regions. Computing via the symmetric half $[H/3,H/2]$ and doubling, using $\sin\alpha=rH,\ \cos\alpha=(1-r)H$:

$$\text{Area}_{\text{zone}}=2\!\left[\frac{r^2-1/9}{2r(1-r)}+\frac{1/2-r}{1-r}\right]=1-\frac{1}{9r(1-r)}\quad(\text{in units of }s^2).$$

So $P(P\text{ in zone})=1-\dfrac{1}{9r(1-r)}$.

Setting this $=53/100$:
$$\frac{1}{9r(1-r)}=\frac{47}{100}\implies r(1-r)=\frac{100}{423}.$$
(Check: $100/423\approx 0.2364\in[2/9,\,1/4]$, so $r\in[1/3,1/2]$. ✓ The other branch $r\le 1/3$ gives $P=1/(3(1-r))=53/100\Rightarrow r=59/159>1/3$, a contradiction—so this is the unique solution.)

**Perimeter probability for $Q$.** Each side has length $s$ with $y$ varying linearly. The zone $[H/3,2H/3]$ intersects each side; the $y$-length of intersection divided by the side's $y$-range gives the fraction:

| Side | $y$-range | Intersection $y$-length | Fraction |
|------|-----------|------------------------|----------|
| $AB$ | $[0,rH]$ | $H(r-1/3)$ | $\dfrac{r-1/3}{r}=1-\dfrac{1}{3r}$ |
| $BC$ | $[rH,H]$ | $H(2/3-r)$ | $\dfrac{2/3-r}{1-r}$ |
| $CD$ | $[(1-r)H,H]$ | $H(r-1/3)$ | $1-\dfrac{1}{3r}$ |
| $DA$ | $[0,(1-r)H]$ | $H(2/3-r)$ | $\dfrac{2/3-r}{1-r}$ |

Total perimeter in zone $=2s\!\left(1-\dfrac{1}{3r}\right)+2s\!\left(\dfrac{2/3-r}{1-r}\right)$, out of total $4s$:

$$P(Q\text{ in zone})=\frac{1}{2}\left[\left(1-\frac{1}{3r}\right)+\frac{2/3-r}{1-r}\right]=\frac{6r(1-r)-1}{6r(1-r)}=1-\frac{1}{6r(1-r)}.$$

**Substituting** $r(1-r)=100/423$:
$$P(Q\text{ in zone})=1-\frac{1}{6\cdot 100/423}=1-\frac{423}{600}=1-\frac{141}{200}=\frac{59}{200}.$$

Since $59$ is prime and $\gcd(59,200)=1$, we have $a=59,\ b=200$.

$$100a+b=100(59)+200=5900+200=\boxed{6100}.$$
